class.name: NetwPersistenceEngine
class.brief_description: One entity's persistence: a frozen persisted-column set over the live scene, and the reads and writes it owes its archetype's database.
class.description:
The scene IS the record. There is no shadow store to keep coherent: a component assigns a property in plain GDScript and the engine reads it at flush time. A column reads and writes the live property on the node that declared it, so a sibling component's persisted field lands in the same row as the root's. [codeblock] # server, in the orphan window Netw.replicate leaves open: var player := PlayerScene.instantiate() var entity := Netw.replicate(player, participant) entity.persistence.hydrate().then( func(_code: Error) -> void: scene.add_child(player)
player.gold += 100 # a plain assignment IS the record; the ) # snapshot loop's next due window # upserts the changed column [/codeblock] [b]Every read and write answers a [NetwPromise], and none of them is a coroutine.[/b] A storage verb cannot answer on the calling frame, and a native caller cannot resume a script coroutine, so the wait lives above this class and never inside it. That is the same boundary [NetwDatabaseBackend] states for the backend it eventually reaches. [NetwEntity] hands one engine out through [member NetwEntity.persistence].

method.name: database
method.description: The effective [NetwDatabase]: the instance override on the entity root when it carries one, otherwise the archetype's declaration, otherwise [code]null[/code]. The override is what lets one packed scene save into a different database per instance, which is how a test gives each case its own storage.

method.name: flush
method.description: Gathers the persisted columns, or the subset named in [param keys], writes them as one merged upsert, and answers a [NetwPromise] resolving with the [enum @GlobalScope.Error] the write reached. Emits [signal flushed] once a write lands. An entity with nothing to write resolves [constant @GlobalScope.OK] without touching the database, so a caller that chains on the answer runs either way. An archetype naming no database or no table resolves [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_UNCONFIGURED], and a database that answers no promise is REJECTED with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_INVALID_DATA] rather than left pending, because a caller waiting on a promise that never settles waits forever. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: hydrate
method.description: Fetches the saved row by [method record_id], applies it onto the live scene properties, emits [signal hydrated], and answers a [NetwPromise] resolving with the [enum @GlobalScope.Error] the read reached. It always settles, including on the paths that apply nothing, so a caller that subscribes is never waiting on an edge that will not come. A missing row resolves [constant @GlobalScope.OK] with the scene defaults intact, because a first play has nothing saved and that is an answer rather than a failure. [b]Server Only.[/b]

method.name: is_dirty
method.description: Whether the live values differ from the last flushed ones. This is the question the snapshot loop asks before spending a write, so a scene nobody touched costs a comparison rather than a transaction.

method.name: owner_node
method.description: The live root of the entity this engine persists, or [code]null[/code] once that entity or its owner is gone. The snapshot loop reads this to decide whether a row still has a body to gather from, so an engine whose owner left the tree drops out of the loop instead of flushing a freed node.

method.name: record_id
method.description: The stable key this entity's row is saved under: the archetype's record-id provider method, else [member NetwEntity.entity_id], else the node name. The node name is the last resort and not a good one, because a scene renames nodes freely and a second instance collides.

signal.name: flushed
signal.description: Emitted after a write landed and its values were adopted as the last flushed state, whether the write came from [method flush] or from the session's snapshot loop.

signal.name: hydrated
signal.description: Emitted after a row is fetched and applied, INCLUDING when no row existed. A first-play entity keeps its scene defaults and still emits, so a listener that places a player on hydration runs on the first play too.
